<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Implement the design of unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing. It utilizes a clock signal (clk), an active-low reset signal (rst_n), an input enable signal (mul_en_in), and provides an output enable signal (mul_en_out) and the product output (mul_out) of size 16 bits.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <logic_description>
        <description>
            Notice that below descriptions are along with tags <![CDATA[ <logic />]]>. These tags <![CDATA[ <logic />]]> could be described more detail in the below description in the <![CDATA[ <implementation />]]> tag.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic" />]]>, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic" />]]> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="sequential_logic" />]]>, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other <![CDATA[ <logic type="sequential_logic" />]]> or <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic" />]]> states.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />]]>, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />]]>, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic id="temp" />]]> tag with width_description and depth_description attributes declaration, such as <![CDATA[ <logic id="temp" width_description="[a:b]" depth_description="[c:d]"/>]]>, it must be declared as `wire [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `combinational_logic`. Otherwise, the logic must be declared as `reg [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `sequential_logic` or a `combinational_logic` driven in a `alway @(*)` block.
        </description>
        <logic type="sequential_logic" id="mul_a_reg">
        8-bit sequential logic.
        If <![CDATA[ <input refid="rst_n" />]]> is deactive, <![CDATA[ <logic refid="mul_a_reg" />]]> is reset to 0.
        Otherwise, <![CDATA[ <logic refid="mul_a_reg" />]]> is set to <![CDATA[ <input refid="mul_a" />]]> if <![CDATA[ <input refid="mul_en_in" />]]> is active, else <![CDATA[ <logic refid="mul_a_reg" />]]> is set to 0.
        </logic>
        <logic type="sequential_logic" id="mul_b_reg">
        8-bit sequential logic.
        If <![CDATA[ <input refid="rst_n" />]]> is deactive, <![CDATA[ <logic refid="mul_b_reg" />]]> is reset to 0.
        Otherwise, <![CDATA[ <logic refid="mul_b_reg" />]]> is set to <![CDATA[ <input refid="mul_b" />]]> if <![CDATA[ <input refid="mul_en_in" />]]> is active, else <![CDATA[ <logic refid="mul_a_reg" />]]> is set to 0.
        </logic>
        <logic type="combinational_logic" id="temp" width_description="[15:0]" depth_description="[7:0]">
        <![CDATA[ <logic refid="temp" />]]> is a logic with 16-bit width and 8-bit depth, `[15:0] temp [7:0]`.
        `temp[0]` is set to value of shift-left-0 of `mul_a_reg` if `mul_b_reg[0]` is active.
        `temp[1]` is set to value of shift-left-1 of `mul_a_reg` if `mul_b_reg[1]` is active.
        etc, ...
        `temp[7]` is set to value of shift-left-7 of `mul_a_reg` if `mul_b_reg[7]` is active.
        </logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>The module utilizes a pipeline architecture to improve performance. It consists of several key components:
Input Control:
The module includes an input enable signal, mul_en_in, which controls the multiplication operation.
On the positive edge of the clock signal, the module samples the input enable signal and stores it in a 3-bit register, mul_en_out_reg.
The value `3-bit` of width of the mul_en_out_reg is assumed that this multiplier has 3 stages. Especifically, on every positive edge of the clock signal, the mul_en_out_reg is concatenated by its previous first two bits and the bit value of the mul_en_in.
The output enable signal, mul_en_out, is derived from the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg, indicating whether the multiplication result is enabled.
If the (rst_n) is inactive, the (mul_en_out) is reset to zero.

Input Registers:
The module includes registers, mul_a_reg and mul_b_reg, to store the input multiplicand and multiplier, respectively.
On the positive edge of the clock signal, the module samples the input values and stores them in the corresponding registers.
The registers are only updated when the input enable signal is active.

Partial Product Generation:
The module generates partial products by performing bitwise operations between the multiplicand and the individual bits of the multiplier.
It uses conditional assignments to select the appropriate bits from the multiplicand based on the multiplier bits.
The partial products are stored in a set of wires, <![CDATA[ <logic refid="temp" />]]>, with each wire <![CDATA[ <logic id="temp" />]]> representing a different bit position.

Partial Sum Calculation:
The module performs addition operations on the partial products to calculate partial sums.
It uses a set of registers, sum, to store the intermediate sum values.
Each register corresponds to a group of partial products and is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal.

Final Product Calculation:
The module sums up all the partial sums to obtain the final product.
It uses a register, mul_out_reg, to store the accumulated sum.
On the positive edge of the clock signal, the register is updated with the sum of all partial sums.

Output Assignment:
The module assigns the output product value, mul_out, based on the output enable signal and the value in mul_out_reg.
If the output enable signal is active, indicating a valid product, the value in mul_out_reg is assigned to mul_out.
Otherwise, mul_out is set to 0.
Notice that the (mul_en_out) is asserted based on the `the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg`. So, to ensure that all the (mul_en_out) and (mul_out) are asserted in the same clock (clk) cycle, the (mul_out) is also asserted based on the `the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg`.
</implementation>
</module>
